brief.recommendation: Waiting costs ~$37,225 in lost checkout revenue and exceeds the 60s business tolerance, while terminating only costs a 2-minute replay (policy may_interrupt). The workload is replayable and may_interrupt. No protected settlements are in flight. No active change-calendar window covers this workload.

audit.report: The batch_replayable_price_sync job (pid 131788) became the root blocker for checkout sessions, causing 12 sessions to wait on locks and driving checkout success down to 25% over the verification window. The trade-off analysis showed waiting would cost ~$37,225 in lost revenue and exceed the 60-second business tolerance, while terminating the workload only required a 2-minute replay. The Database Guardian and Continuity Guardian both confirmed the workload is replayable, may_interrupt, and has no protected settlements or active change-calendar windows. The pact agreed to terminate in 2 rounds over 39.4 seconds, but the verifier found the database still had 12 sessions waiting on locks and checkout SLO at 25%, marking the outcome ESCALATED.
audit.root_cause: batch_replayable_price_sync (pid 131788) entered an idle-in-transaction state and blocked checkout sessions, causing checkout success to drop to 25% and leaving 12 sessions waiting on locks.
lessons: For batch_replayable_price_sync: verify protected_settlements and change_calendar invariants before proposing terminate, as the Continuity Guardian requires these checks even when the workload is marked may_interrupt.
Add a runtime guard that auto-terminates batch_replayable_price_sync after 60 seconds of idle-in-transaction to prevent checkout revenue loss from exceeding the business tolerance.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians efficiently weighed the trade-off: the Database Guardian quantified the $37k+ waiting cost against the 2-minute replay cost, and the Continuity Guardian confirmed the interrupt policy and invariants before accepting termination, avoiding a wasted round.
follow_ups: Review the batch_replayable_price_sync job definition to ensure the may_interrupt and replay_cost flags are documented and enforced by the scheduler.
Add a dashboard alert when a batch job holds an idle-in-transaction lock for >30s, triggering an automatic trade-off re-evaluation.
Confirm with the pricing team that the 2-minute replay cost for price_sync is accurate and that no downstream dependencies will break on replay.
